messages:
alex: Heads up — since ~10:12 we saw NVMe write latency spike on gpu-spot-* hosts after the batch job ramp. Ephemeral-cleaner CPU and IO went to 100% and I saw a bunch of OOM killer logs for cleaner pods.

maria: Grafana panel (https://grafana.internal/r/abc123) shows write latency P99 from 8ms -> 120ms, IOPS steady but qdepth rising. Which pool?

alex: It's the gpu-batch-pool in us-west1. Affected nodes: gpu-spot-42, gpu-spot-43, gpu-spot-44. dmesg shows repeated nvme timeout + device requeue entries.

sam: @alex @maria I'm oncall — running iostat now
```
Device             tps    kB_read/s    kB_wrtn/s    kB_read    kB_wrtn
nvme0n1           8500        12.00      15324.00   1200000   153240000
```
Looks like sustained write throughput + high await. Cleaner is writing temp data + GC.

ops-bot: Incident bot: Created INC-2026-451 in #incidents (priority P2) — assigned to infra-oncall.

jin: Quick mitigation: reduce ephemeral-cleaner concurrency and increase trim interval. Patch (daemonset):
```
kubectl patch ds ephemeral-cleaner -n infra --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/0/value","value":"2"}]'
```
Also lowering --max-writers to 2 and bumping --scrub-interval to 15m.

alex: Applied patch to canary nodes (gpu-spot-42). Observing iostat: qdepth dropped ~40% and write latency P99 dropped from 120ms -> 28ms in ~60s. Good signal.

maria: Long term: consider rate-limit of background writes to avoid competing with GPU batch checkpoint writes. Also schedule a maintenance to replay firmware nvme scrub on nodes with requeues.

sam: Created infra ticket TOOLS-987 to track runbook + config defaults. Also proposing spot pool autoscale to avoid bursting beyond local-disk capacity. cc @product for cost impact (moving batch to dedicated increases monthly cost).

alex: Thanks. I'll keep the canary patched and run full rollout if stable. If anyone sees requeues again ping @oncall.

maria: :thumbsup:
